$comment: Source of truth for the models the web app loads. Editing this file is how you deploy a
retrained model — no JavaScript changes needed. Drop the .onnx next to this file, update
`file`, `labels` and `imgsz` to match what you exported, and the app picks it up.
A model whose `file` is missing or fails to load is reported in the UI as unavailable;
the app stays usable for whatever else did load. Keep every file well under ~15 MB — it
downloads to the visitor's browser. Export with `python3 tools/export_onnx.py`, which

gate.description: Routes an upload to the right analysis, or rejects it.

turbine.notes: Awaiting a model. Set labels to match the export (tools/export_onnx.py writes them from the model), and severityWeights to one entry per label - higher means more serious. Both described the previous dataset's three surface classes and were cleared with it.

solar.notes: RGB only. Cannot detect hotspots, cell defects, bypass-diode failure or offline modules - those are electrical faults visible only in thermal infrared.
solar.zeroDetectionNote: Found none of the visible-light defect classes. RGB cannot show hotspots, cell defects, bypass-diode failure or offline modules; those need thermal infrared.

crowd.notes: Regions under pressure, not individual people. At event density a person is a few pixels wide and overlaps their neighbours, so no model can box them one by one, and a number would read as a count this image cannot support.
crowd.zeroDetectionNote: None of the pressure patterns above were found in this frame. That is a null result about this frame only: it is not a finding that the crowd is safe, and conditions change faster than any single image.

wildfire.notes: One frame from one angle. Fire behind a smoke column, inside a treeline or under canopy does not appear from above, and a person the camera cannot resolve is the normal case rather than a rare one.
wildfire.zeroDetectionNote: Nothing in the list above was found in this frame. That describes this frame and nothing else - not the ground under the smoke, not what is inside the treeline, and not whether anyone is there.
